relevance_note: Case report of one woman with SSADH deficiency and two ALDH5A1 variants: "Here, we present a patient with a severe phenotype of SSADHD caused by a novel genetic variant c.728T > C".
method_note: Read and transcribed by hand; a short script only assembled the JSON and checked spans. Scope: the index patient plus two relatives described with features (father: recurrent seizures; paternal uncle: autism spectrum disorder), neither reported as tested. The 'healthy brother' (not tested, not affected) and the mother (only her family history described) get no rows. Table 2 lists 62 literature missense variants by source reference without any individual-level data, so no literature persons were extracted. Table 1 is a FoldX stability table (not patient data). Transcript NM_001080.3 is taken from Methods 4.1, which says the variant description corresponds to it. Zygosity: Results say 'heterozygosity for a known missense variant, c.278G > T' and Discussion calls c.728T > C 'novel heterozygous', but Discussion states 'compound heterozygosity' for the two variants; recorded compound heterozygous. Parents gave consent for genetic analysis but no parental testing result is reported, so inheritance and parental testing are not reported. Dystonia not recorded: the paper hedges ('probably due to a mild generalized dystonia or a more unspecific “central tone-coordination disorder”'). Dyspraxia not recorded ('possibly some features of dyspraxia'). Intellectual disability checklist left not reported: the paper says cognitive abilities are 'heterogeneous and impaired by autistic and possibly some features of dyspraxia' (recorded as a free-text feature) rather than intellectual disability. Ataxia left not reported: wide-based gait is attributed to hypotonia and leg stiffening 'without further cerebellar signs'. Vital status 'alive' rests on 'The patient, now aged 23 years, suffers from...'. Age at diagnosis (biochemical, 'at the age of two years') converted to P2Y. cites_prior_report_of_same_patients left null: no statement either way. Typo in paper: 'p.Le243Pro' in the FoldX paragraph; 'p.Lys118Arn' in Table 2 (not extracted). No contradictions about the patient's features found.
